changes: Batch and single-AIR GPU provers transfer each opened field vector into the established native proof type without cloning its allocation; the final permutation commitment is moved by ownership.

A shared consuming assembler accounts for incoming capacities at every nested vector level and admits layout metadata, preprocessing validation scratch, native instance descriptors and quotient-row descriptors together against the existing host-output allowance.

Exact fallible descriptor vectors preserve field-vector pointers, lengths and capacities; preprocessing matrices may be reordered and sparse, and quotient ranges must completely partition their opening round.
Non-Clone drop-counted fixtures test ownership and rejection cleanup. Capacity, combined-boundary, malformed-layout, overflow, optional-round and frozen-encoding checks cover the handoff.
Quadratic legacy wallets, cubic block-v2 wallets and three-AIR batches verify after GPU shutdown; seeded multi-AIR proofs match the CPU reference with and without device randomness and transcripts.
Two archived full-size finalizers preserve registry identity and arithmetic operation counts, completing all 16 arithmetic stages on OpenCL and passing independent CPU verification.

qualification_attempts.reason: Controller multi-AIR selector matched zero cases; all completed handoff unit and wallet tests passed. No source change is required.

limitations: Handoff admission occurs after PCS opening and proof generation have produced their outputs. It is not whole-proof preflight and does not roll back earlier GPU, randomness or transcript work.

The handoff census covers nested opened-value capacities and all new descriptors. The FRI opening proof, commitment caps, lookup terminals, caller-owned metadata, allocator overhead and engine/driver storage require their enclosing reservations.

Owned field allocations retain their spare capacity rather than shrinking. The default host-output maximum remains 32 GiB; qualification explicitly sets 3 GiB. The independent FRI proof-query allowance remains 1 GiB.
The 3 GiB worker, 4 GiB aggregate host, 7 GiB managed GPU and 1 GiB device-allocation caps are unchanged. No allowance is inferred from an observed peak.
Ordinary pool admission still rejects the qualification profile without complete lifetime phases. Isolated finalizer timings do not establish throughput or a performance gain.

Complete native proof lifetimes, CPU verification scratch, full scheduler phase integration, broader and nonempty-child workloads, sustained throughput, multiple GPUs and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
